# Execution Trace Summary

The harness demonstrates **poor learning across all three datasets**, with training accuracy ranging from 32–42% and evaluation accuracy between 48–52%, indicating the in-context few-shot approach is not effectively capturing underlying patterns. The model produces generic reasoning statements across failures (e.g., "Closest demonstrations suggest X"), suggesting shallow pattern matching rather than genuine understanding of the task structure. A recurring failure mode is selecting plausible but incorrect outputs from the available label space, particularly when evaluation context grows beyond ~7.7KB—ds_alpha achieves the best eval accuracy (52%) with a compact context, while ds_beta drops to 48% despite triple the context size and explicit multiple-choice options. Memory state balloons monotonically through training without corresponding performance gains, and the single LLM call per eval step cannot correct misaligned predictions. To improve, focus on whether the prompt structure adequately conveys the underlying decision rule versus simply aggregating surface-level token similarities.
